name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
short_status: Success: landed 17 November 1970; Lunokhod 1 became the first rover on another world, drove ~10 km over 11 lunar days, and its laser reflector has been answering Earth again since 2010.
tagline: Soviet Union · Rover · 1970 · The space race Success
stats: rover ever to drive on another world
official odometry (9.93 km per the 2013 LRO remap)
operated, against a three-day design life
returned by its laser reflector on the first 2010 shot, after 39 years of silence

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 17 November 1970, 03:46:50 UT, Sea of Rains (Mare Imbrium) at 38.23764 N, 35.00163 W; rover rolled down dual ramps to the surface

facts.label: LROC-derived coordinates (+/- ~15 m)
facts.value: Luna 17 lander: 38.2376 N, 324.9984 E; Lunokhod 1 final position: 38.3151 N, 324.9919 E

facts.label: Rover
facts.value: 756 kg, about 1.35 m high and 2.15 m across, eight independently powered wheels (Siddiqi, NASA SP-2018-4041)

facts.label: Power and survival
facts.value: Solar array under the hinged lid by day; polonium-210 radioisotope heater through the two-week lunar night

facts.label: Design life vs actual
facts.value: Intended to operate three lunar days; operated eleven; operations officially ceased 4 October 1971, the anniversary of Sputnik 1

facts.label: Traverse
facts.value: 10,540 m per the official Soviet odometry; 9.93 km per the 2013 LRO-image cartographic reconstruction

facts.label: Science return
facts.value: More than 20,000 TV pictures, more than 200 TV panoramas, more than 500 lunar soil tests (plus X-ray spectrometer, X-ray telescope, cosmic-ray detectors)

facts.label: Rediscovery
facts.value: Luna 17 and rover tracks identified in LROC images published 17 March 2010; rover itself imaged at its final parking spot

facts.label: Laser ranging revival
facts.value: 22 April 2010: APOLLO team (Tom Murphy, UCSD) hits the reflector with the Apache Point 3.5 m telescope, ~2,000 photons returned on the first try after almost 40 years of silence

facts.label: Reflector performance
facts.value: French-built retroreflector returns a signal roughly four times stronger than Lunokhod 2's; position now known to few-centimeter accuracy

timeline: 03:46:50 UT: Luna 17 soft-lands in Mare Imbrium; Lunokhod 1 rolls down the ramps, the first wheels on another world
Rover falls silent after eleven lunar days; operations officially cease 4 October 1971, the Sputnik 1 anniversary
LROC publishes images identifying Luna 17 and the rover's tracks on Mare Imbrium
Apache Point laser ranging gets ~2,000 photons back from the reflector on the first attempt
LROC low-altitude pass (33 km) images Lunokhod 1 parked at 38.315 N, 324.992 E
LRO-based cartographic reconstruction remeasures the traverse at 9.93 km, about 0.5 km less than the official 10.54 km
